summary: Defines how iSCSI hosts, devices, and management services use the Service Location Protocol (SLP), with SLP service type templates describing their services, so iSCSI targets and name servers can be found.

eli5.summary: It's a way for computers to ask the network, where are the storage drives, and get an answer.

questions: how do iscsi initiators discover targets
what is the iscsi default tcp port
subtitle: How iSCSI initiators can find storage targets and management servers on a network without per-host configuration, using SLPv2.

tldr.problem: An iSCSI initiator normally needs each target, or each address offering targets, configured by hand. Finding targets and name services without configuring every initiator is desirable.
tldr.mechanism: Targets and storage management servers register with the Service Location Protocol (SLPv2) using three service type templates, and initiators query SLP with attribute filters to find them.
tldr.outcome: Initiators can discover targets and management services automatically. RFC 4018 is a Proposed Standard and is updated by RFC 7146.

facts.label: SLP transport required
facts.value: SLP over TCP MUST be implemented

today: RFC 4018 is a Proposed Standard and is updated by RFC 7146. It has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: Why Use SLP for iSCSI
sections.content:
iSCSI carries SCSI commands, data and status across an IP network over TCP. The client end is an initiator that sends commands, and the server end is a target that runs them.

Two ways to find targets need no SLP: configure each target and its address on the initiator, or configure each address that provides targets and ask it for a list. Both require some configuration on every initiator. RFC 4018 describes how the Service Location Protocol (SLP, RFC 2608) can be used instead to discover targets, addresses providing targets, and storage management servers. It assumes SLPv2 and does not cover SLPv1.
sections.eli5: Instead of writing down where every storage drive lives for every computer, the drives announce themselves and computers just ask who is out there.

sections.title: SLP Roles and iSCSI Terms
sections.content:
SLP has three roles. A User Agent (UA) works for the client and retrieves service information. A Service Agent (SA) advertises services and their capabilities. A Directory Agent (DA) collects service advertisements. A scope is a named set of services, typically a logical administrative group, and a service advertisement is a URL, attributes and a lifetime.

On the iSCSI side, an iSCSI Client includes at least one initiator, and an iSCSI Server includes at least one target. Each target holds one or more Logical Units, each of which is a SCSI device such as a disk or tape drive. Every initiator and target has an iSCSI Name, a UTF-8 string that serves as its unique identifier.
sections.eli5: Some helpers shout what they offer, some ask what is available, and some keep a notice board. The storage side has computers that ask and drives that answer.

sections.title: Discovering iSCSI Targets
sections.content:
An iSCSI client runs an SLP UA, and an iSCSI server runs an SLP SA. The server registers a service:iscsi:target advertisement for every combination of target and network address, each with a lifetime and the attributes from the template. An iSCSI target URL consists of a host name or IP address, the TCP port and the iSCSI name. In the RFC's example the server listens on TCP port 3260 at two addresses and has targets named one, two and three, so six service URLs are registered, such as 192.0.2.131:3260/one.

The procedure is the ordinary SLP one. If a DA is found, the SA registers with it, and the SA also answers multicast UA queries directly. The UA contacts the DA by unicast or the SA by multicast, or an SA by unicast if its address is configured. The UA includes an attribute query describing the targets it needs. With the host, port and target name in hand, the initiator starts the normal iSCSI login.

Because template information may exceed common datagram sizes, UAs and SAs supporting this template MUST implement SLP over TCP. Where multicast is unavailable or not allowed, such as public or service-provider networks between two iSCSI gateways, an initiator can be configured with SA addresses and send unicast requests directly.
sections.eli5: Each drive posts a card for every door it can be reached through. A computer asks the notice board, or shouts to the room, then walks to the right door and knocks.

sections.title: Finding Targets by Initiator Credentials
sections.content:
A target may require an initiator to present an iSCSI initiator name, an IP address, a CHAP, SRP or Kerberos credential, or a combination. Ideally an initiator would get replies only for targets where login is guaranteed to succeed, so the target template carries three list-valued attributes: auth-name (allowed initiator names), auth-addr (allowed host names or IP addresses) and auth-cred (allowed method/identifier credentials). Each can hold the value any when nothing specific is required.

Some targets allow several identities, and a single registration cannot say that name A goes with credential A while name B goes with credential B. Such a target is registered under more than one service URL, each with an extra opaque identity string after the iSCSI name, separated by a /. Because these attributes describe security policy, IPsec MUST be implemented if they are distributed.
sections.eli5: A club can list who is allowed in on its card. A kid searches for clubs that let their name in, so they do not waste time at doors that will stay shut.

sections.title: Storage Management Services
sections.content:
Storage management servers can manage and control access to targets and offer extras such as storage allocation. RFC 4018 defines none of those services; it only lets them be discovered. A management server advertises itself as service:iscsi:sms with a URL holding its domain name or IP address and a TCP or UDP port number.

The roles flip compared with target discovery: iSCSI clients and servers both run UAs, and the management server runs the SA. A target may also let the management service register its targets on its behalf, so a target device does not have to advertise itself. This has no impact on the initiator, so target discovery works the same whether or not a management service exists or who registers the targets.
sections.eli5: Besides drives, there can be a helper who manages them. The helper posts a card too, and both computers and drives can look it up.

sections.title: The Three SLP Templates
sections.content:
RFC 4018 provides three templates, each registered as template-version=1.0. The abstract service:iscsi template is the top level that encloses all iSCSI services. The concrete service:iscsi:target template registers individual target addresses, and its URL path is hostport "/" iscsi-name [ "/" identity ].

Besides the auth-* attributes, the target template has iscsi-name, portal-group (addresses sharing a name and portal group tag can be used in the same iSCSI session), transports, mgmt-entity, alias and boot-list (initiators that may boot from the target). Typical queries find a target by name, such as (iscsi-name=iqn.2001-04.com.example:sn.456), or find targets open to a given initiator or to any.

The service:iscsi:sms template has a protocols attribute whose listed value is isns, a transports attribute, and server-priority, which tells a client which of several servers to prefer. With iSNS the primary server has the lowest value, 0.
sections.eli5: The templates are fill-in-the-blank cards. One form is for drives, one is for helpers, and one big heading says they all belong to the same family.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The SLPv2 security model gives UAs a way to check that advertisements come from trusted SAs, but gives no confidentiality and cannot authenticate zero-result responses. Once a service is found, authentication and authorization are handled by iSCSI or by the management server's own protocol. Without SLP security there is a risk of false discovery information, and IPsec and iSCSI in-band authentication SHOULD be used when that risk matters, so an attacker claiming to be a target lacks the secrets to finish authentication.

A denial of service risk remains, because false information can trigger repeated IKE negotiation. Three measures MUST be implemented: IP address range limits, DNS domain limits and a negative authentication cache. The auth-name, auth-addr, auth-cred and boot-list attributes are security policy information. If IPsec is not implemented they MUST NOT be distributed via SLPv2 and MUST NOT be used if discovered that way. SLPv2 authentication itself is OPTIONAL to implement and use.
sections.eli5: Anyone can pin a fake card on the board, so a drive still checks who you are at the door. And the secret lists of who may enter stay hidden unless the notes are locked in an envelope.

sections.title: IANA Registration
sections.content: The three templates were reviewed and approved by the IESG and registered in the IANA "SVRLOC Templates" registry, following the process in the IANA Considerations of RFC 2609.
sections.eli5: The three forms were filed in an official cabinet so everyone uses the same ones.

viz.caption: THE THREE iSCSI SLP SERVICE TYPES

items.title: service:iscsi
items.text: Abstract type that encloses all iSCSI-related services.

items.title: service:iscsi:target
items.text: Registers each target at each address, with auth-* and boot-list attributes.

items.title: service:iscsi:sms
items.text: Registers a storage management server, with a protocols list and server-priority.
